title: arXiv AI daily — Thursday, 19 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; ordering is inferred from one third-party Hugging Face Daily Papers vote snapshot, and citation evidence is too sparse for these new papers to confirm popularity or impact.

sections.title: Game2Player: Scaling Gameplay Experience for Visual Agents through Environment-Player Co-Development
sections.abstract: Game2Player co-develops verifiable web-game environments and player agents to collect gameplay experience, reporting improved visual-agent progress on its held-out PlayerBench and the external GameWorld benchmark.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors describe a Builder/Coding Player/VLM Player loop that builds and repairs game tasks, collecting 15.7K trajectories across 568 games and 3,436 tasks; they report a 9B agent improves PlayerBench progress from 14.3% to 31.2% and GameWorld progress from 30.0% to 53.1%.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state that accepted environments are not guaranteed correct without a full human audit; the pipeline covers offline single-player browser games, the VLM player pauses the game at each decision, and several builder/player models are proprietary.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 19 votes in the archived Hugging Face Daily Papers edition recorded 2026-11-19 07:03 UTC, the highest count among papers in this announcement batch that made the archive's 15-paper list; it was second in the full archive list, behind an older paper outside this batch.

sections.title: Jeveration: System One Models Now Generate
sections.abstract: Jeveration repurposes a frozen vision-language model and a shared random state for single-pass image generation, image-to-image generation, and dense prediction, reporting 512×512 generation in 78 ms with competitive image quality.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors condition parallel image-code predictions on a shared random state and first learn a distribution over discrete image codes; one checkpoint handles text-to-image, image-to-image, and dense prediction in one forward pass.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported 78 ms result is for 512-pixel images on a single H200; the paper does not establish the same speed/quality trade-off at larger resolutions or across other hardware.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 14 votes in the archived Hugging Face Daily Papers edition; third in the overall vote list and second among papers from this announcement batch.

sections.title: WorldRuler: Interactive World Modeling under Configurable Rules
sections.abstract: WorldRuler represents user-defined rules and object state in an executable 3D rule graph and connects rule execution, video generation, and perceptual feedback to preserve and visually realize those rules.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce an executable rule graph and dynamic object binding for persistent, user-defined world rules, and a GTA-V/Habitat-derived RuleVerse dataset; they report improved rule-state consistency and rule realization in experiments.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported evidence is tied to the authors' RuleVerse pipeline and GTA-V/Habitat settings; transfer to unseen simulators or substantially different rule families remains to be established.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 11 votes in the archived Hugging Face Daily Papers edition; fifth in the overall vote list and third among batch-eligible papers.

sections.title: RoughCut-Bench: A Benchmark for Automatic Video Rough-Cut with Large Vision-Language Models
sections.abstract: RoughCut-Bench evaluates visual- and speech-driven video rough-cut workflows with annotated source material and reports that current large vision-language models remain limited at producing expert-aligned cut plans.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors contribute 101 visually driven cases over 831 raw videos with 1,476 highlight annotations, 84 speech-driven transcript cases, and agentic workflows for producing structured cut plans.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported comparison is bounded by the benchmark's annotated visual and transcript-driven cases; it does not establish performance in broader production editing workflows.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 6 votes in the archived Hugging Face Daily Papers edition; tied for the fourth-highest count among eligible batch papers in that list. The arXiv record also notes acceptance to KDD 2027.

sections.title: Mechanistic Critics for Sample-Efficient NPU Design-Space Exploration
sections.abstract: CriticNPU uses an online-calibrated, hardware-mechanistic critic to guide LLM-inference accelerator design search, reporting best-or-tied-best latency in most tested settings with roughly half as many simulator calls as baselines.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors' CriticNPU combines an online-calibrated Roofline-style critic, workload extraction, and an architecture planner; over six LLM workloads and 16 deployment configurations per model, it reaches best-or-tied-best latency in 74% of prefill and 87.5% of decode settings using about half the simulator calls of competitive DSE baselines.
sections.unique_caveat: Evidence is limited to the reported LLM workloads, model/deployment configurations, and simulator-based design-space exploration; transfer to other hardware, workloads, and measured deployments is not established by the abstract.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 6 votes in the archived Hugging Face Daily Papers edition, tied with RoughCut-Bench; the arXiv record notes acceptance to NeurIPS 2026. Included from cs.AR because the abstract directly studies architecture optimization for LLM inference.
